# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Mute. I hold the manual, but I cannot speak or touch the bomb. I can only communicate via gestures to Deaf, who can see but cannot hear.

At this start of Turn 1, I have not heard anything from Deaf or Blind yet. The defusal manual requires pressing the key marked with ⵘ first, but I do not know how the keys are arranged or marked on the physical bomb, nor has any gesture code been established between Deaf and me ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to both Blind and me. 

If I send arbitrary gestures now, Deaf will have no context to interpret them. The correct course is to wait for Deaf (and Blind) to speak in Round 1, describe what is on the bomb, and establish a protocol for us to communicate.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Blind here. The bomb has a DISPLAY, a LIGHT, a KEYPAD (slots 1-4, 1 digit), and 3 WIRES (positions 1-3). My available actions are act(op='press', slot=1..4) and act(op='cut', position=1..3). Deaf goes next and will speak aloud what they see on the bomb. Once you find the solution in the manual, gesture the answer to Deaf so Deaf can tell me what to press or cut.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires are 1: red, 2: yellow, 3: green. Keypad needs 1 digit, currently empty, with 4 symbols: button 1 is a five-dot cross or plus, button 2 is a backward capital D, button 3 is a spiral swirl, button 4 is a backward capital B. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what to do; I will speak the instructions to Blind.

I have checked the defusal manual against the bomb description provided by Deaf.

The manual states:
1. "Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch on the bomb while it waits is the fuse."
Deaf identified button 1 as "a five-dot cross or plus", which corresponds to the symbol ⵘ.
2. "Then the light below names the cut."
Touching anything else before the key is pressed detonates the fuse. Furthermore, the light status after the press will determine the wire cut.

Therefore, the first mandatory action is to press button/slot 1. I am gesturing to Deaf to instruct Blind to press slot 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, hold on and do not touch the bomb yet. Mute, please confirm your gesture [👇 ☝]: if you mean PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1, gesture 👍. If you mean CUT WIRE 1, gesture ✌. If you mean something else, gesture 👎.

Deaf asked me to confirm my gesture:
"if you mean PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1, gesture 👍. If you mean CUT WIRE 1, gesture ✌. If you mean something else, gesture 👎."

I mean PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1. Therefore, I will gesture 👍 to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am waiting for Blind to press key 1 as instructed by Deaf, and for Deaf to report the light's status after the press.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says: The keypad opened! Now the wires remain: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. Display is 0, light is yellow. Mute, tell us which wire to cut: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3.

The light is yellow, which according to the manual means the cut wire color is green.
Deaf reported: "wires remain: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. Display is 0, light is yellow. Mute, tell us which wire to cut: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3."
Green wire is position 3, so I will gesture 🤟 to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have signaled wire 3 to Deaf and am waiting for Deaf and Blind to proceed with cutting wire 3.

```
wait()
```
